decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm comparing speed tiers—Dragapult's base 142 speed likely outpaces Mega Garchomp even with its stat boosts, since Sand Force drops Mega Garchomp's speed to around 92 base.

Running the damage math, a Dragon Claw from Mega Garchomp's boosted attack looks like it OHKOs Dragapult even accounting for its decent bulk, while Dragapult's Dragon Darts probably only deal 60-70% back, so Garchomp should survive the exchange—megaevolving for the power seems worth the minor speed tradeoff here.

Scarf Gholdengo Shadow Ball for Dragapult (Life Orb, U-turn, 90%). Incineroar is at 28% with Fake Out; keep Kingambit away from Incineroar's Fire moves.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm calculating Dragon Claw damage from a -1 Atk Mega Garchomp against Dragonite, factoring in its defense stat, STAB, and the super-effective multiplier, then halving the result for Multiscale.

Stone Edge from Garchomp does even less without STAB. Switching out would reset Garchomp's Atk drop though, so I'm weighing Gholdengo as a safer answer—it resists Dragon and can threaten back with Make It Rain, though Dragonite's bulk and Multiscale mean it'll take two hits to bring down regardless of which attacker I use.

Kingambit also looks appealing since it resists both Dragon and Flying and brings Sucker Punch/Swords Dance pressure, while Iron Head from Dragonite against it deals relatively little in return.

Weighing the matchup further, Kingambit's higher bulk means it survives an Earthquake from Dragonite better than Gholdengo would, though Incineroar's Fake Out plus Fire-type pressure still needs accounting for against Kingambit's typing.

decisions.thought: Plan: Dragonite +1+1 full HP Multiscale intact. EQ Kingambit now without Mega to keep Multiscale tanking. Mega later after Multiscale breaks to sweep. Mega Garchomp 72% -1 still threat. Keep Incineroar 28% for later Intimidate. Pult healthy.

decisions.thought: Dragonite +1/+1 (likely Multiscale, unknown item); Kowtow Cleave to break Multiscale. Then Garchomp Stone Edge (~174 dmg unscaled) should KO the weakened Dragonite. Watch for an Earthquake/Fire Punch from Dragonite on Kingambit. Dragapult 90% Life Orb with U-turn: scarf Gholdengo Shadow Ball. Incineroar 28% with Fake Out: Garchomp EQ.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking whether a +1 Dragonite with Multiscale at full HP can threaten Kingambit with Earthquake, estimating the damage roughly against Kingambit's bulk to see if it's a meaningful hit.

I'm also weighing Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave against Dragonite's Multiscale, concluding it doesn't deal enough to be decisive, and then considering alternative switch-ins like Gholdengo and Garchomp to see how they'd handle Dragonite's speed and coverage moves, including Garchomp's Stone Edge against the Multiscale buffer.

Weighing whether Kingambit should Sucker Punch immediately to break Multiscale versus setting up Swords Dance first, I'm running rough damage math either way and finding neither option cleanly secures the win before Dragonite's EQ chips Kingambit down too far.

Checking if Gholdengo's Make It Rain can finish off Dragonite after Sucker Punch breaks multiscale—looks like it should get the KO at around 70% damage. Then weighing whether Garchomp's Stone Edge could clean up instead, though switching Garchomp in risks eating a hit first.

Comparing Sucker Punch versus Kowtow Cleave for Kingambit: Sucker Punch breaks multiscale but fails if Dragonite sets up again with Dragon Dance, while Kowtow Cleave hits reliably regardless and also lowers Kingambit's defense as a bonus, making it the safer choice against another DD.

decisions.thought: Plan: KO 21% Kingambit with EQ. Mega now since Multiscale broken for power/speed to sweep Mega Garchomp 72% -1 and last mon. Keep Pult healthy, Incineroar 28% for later Intimidate. Watch Rotom-Wash Levitate EQ immune.

decisions.thought: Kingambit is at 45 HP and slower than Dragonite (+1/+1, at 69%, has EQ and DD). Sucker Punch for chip (~25%). After it faints: Garchomp Stone Edge or scarf Gholdengo Make It Rain (scarf outspeeds +1 Dragonite) to finish it. Dragapult 90% Life Orb with U-turn: Gholdengo Shadow Ball. Incineroar 28% with Fake Out: Garchomp EQ.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Kingambit at 45 HP, Dragonite's next EQ should finish it off, and even a Sucker Punch would only deal around 25%, leaving Kingambit short of a KO before it falls. I'm also considering switching to Garchomp since it's immune to Earthquake, though Dragonite could pivot to Extreme Speed or Dragon-type coverage instead.

Weighing Gholdengo as a switch-in, it's risky since a boosted Earthquake would nearly one-shot it given its Defense. Garchomp handles the dragon move fine but isn't immune to Earthquake since it's Ground-type, not Ground-immune, so that trade is roughly neutral damage.

I think the cleanest line is firing off Sucker Punch now to chip Dragonite before Kingambit faints, then bringing in Garchomp to try to outspeed and finish with Stone Edge, though the exact math on whether that OHKOes is close given Dragonite's boosted bulk.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo (scarf, 223 speed) goes in on Dragonite (20%, +1/+1, Mega, EQ, DD) and uses Make It Rain to KO it. It is immune to Extreme Speed. Next, Shadow Ball the Dragapult (90%, Life Orb, U-turn), switching first to reset the choice lock if needed. Garchomp EQ for Incineroar (28%, Fake Out). Garchomp 134/185.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Checking speed tiers: mega Dragonite at +1 could reach around 250 speed, which outpaces scarf Gholdengo's boosted 223 and definitely beats Garchomp's 158. Gholdengo is weak to Earthquake as a Steel type, so a +1 mega Dragonite with EQ would hit it hard, while Garchomp takes it neutrally.

Gholdengo locked into Make It Rain would drop to -1 SpA after, but Dragapult doesn't resist Steel so that's fine. The real safety is Extreme Speed being useless against Gholdengo's Ghost typing, making it the safer send-in overall.

Dragapult (90%, Life Orb, U-turn): Gholdengo Shadow Ball after a reset, or Garchomp Dragon Claw. Garchomp 134/185.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Comparing speed tiers with scarf Gholdengo at 223 against Mega Dragonite's boosted speed range, I'm unsure which outspeeds. Make It Rain at 120 BP hits Dragonite hard since Multiscale would already be broken, dealing significant damage even neutral against Steel.

But Dragonite's Earthquake is 4x against Gholdengo given its typing, and comparing to a similar Kingambit scenario, that attack would likely knock Gholdengo out at full HP if it survives to strike back. Weighing Shadow Ball instead — it keeps special attack unboosted and sets up nicely for a follow-up against Dragapult, with damage estimates putting it around 36-45 HP depending on Dragonite's SpD roll, which combined with the 20% Multiscale-broken health should be enough to finish it off while leaving a better matchup for the next threat.

decisions.thought: Dragon Claw to KO Dragonite (20%, +1/+1 Mega, Earthquake, Dragon Dance). Next targets: Incineroar (28%, Fake Out, Intimidate) with Earthquake, and Dragapult (90%, Life Orb, U-turn) with Dragon Claw. Garchomp is my last mon at 134/185. Its Attack drop reset when it switched out.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Garchomp's stat drops reset when it switched out earlier, so it's back to neutral now. Dragonite is faster and at 20% HP but its Dragon-type move at +1 could still knock out Garchomp given its HP total, and we can't outspeed to prevent that.

Dragon Claw has 100% accuracy and should easily finish off the 20% Dragonite if Garchomp survives, so that's safer than relying on Stone Edge's 80% accuracy.
